doc.title: Tom Albert and Milton "Mooney" Martin Interview, 1964-12-21

title: The murder of a boy near Solace's grocery
summary: Martin and Tom tell of a local killing: an eleven-year-old killed a ten-year-old and hid him in a ditch, and the body was found when buzzards circled. They then trail off into talk about Harry and his trumpet-playing father.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: I was a half. You take... That's when Chuck killed John. Yeah. You remember? Who was that guy selling that house on that track?

That's old man Solace. That's right. He killed a... He was eleven years old and John was ten and he killed him. And put him in the caddy. Dragged him in the ditch. In the ditch. In the ditch. And covered him up with the... With the grass, right? Yeah. And they did nobody know why he was.
Until the buzzards was swollen over. And they found him. And that was why they went there and found him in the ditch. Yeah.
Who was that guy? I don't know.
Oh, Harry, the old man used to blow trumpet there. Oh yeah, that's right. Harry, his son. His son. That's right.
His mother named Elizabeth. That's right.

And he lived over here, then he come over here afterwards. Then he come over here and right here. When I got big enough, you can call him Al Jays, when I got big enough, he cut Willie Jones right here on this corner. Yeah, 12 little fella.
